Since Bun 1.4.3, `fetch()` rejects with the system's error code. `ConnectionRefused` is `ECONNREFUSED`, or a more specific code like `EHOSTUNREACH`.

`--fix` replaces `ConnectionRefused` in files that call `fetch()`. `Bun.S3Client` still uses the old code, so in a file that has both, or neither, it's a suggestion.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/no-legacy-fetch-error-codes" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
try {
  await fetch(url);
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === "ConnectionRefused") retry();
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
try {
  await fetch(url);
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === "ECONNREFUSED") retry();
}
```

A function that checks for both codes works on every version:

{/* good */}
```ts
const isRefused = error => error.code === "ECONNREFUSED" || error.code === "ConnectionRefused";
```
